sections.domain: Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles
sections.heading: C2 — Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A101
Leave at least three feet when passing a bicycle, and increase passing clearance at higher speeds. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A101
Wait until opposing traffic is visible and a pass is safe before moving partly or fully into the other lane to pass a cyclist. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A101
To confirm a cyclist notices the vehicle, wave or nod and wait for a response. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A101
Avoid sounding the horn close to a cyclist because it can startle the rider into an unexpected action. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A101
Before opening the driver's door after parallel parking, verify that no cyclist is approaching. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A101
Reach across the body with the opposite hand for the door handle, using the resulting turn to check the mirror and over the shoulder for cyclists. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A101
Use turn signals to make intended turns and lane changes predictable to cyclists and drivers. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A101
Do not park in or block a bicycle lane, which is a designated cyclist travel lane. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A101
A sharrow is a shared-lane pavement marking indicating a preferred cycling position within the travel lane. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A102
Shared-lane markings help cyclists position themselves where a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and motor vehicle to travel side by side. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A102
A shared-lane marking alerts road users to cyclists' likely position, encourages safe passing and discourages wrong-way cycling. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A102
A Bicycles May Use Full Lane sign can supplement or replace shared-lane markings. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A103
Motorcyclists have the same highway rights, responsibilities and traffic-law obligations as other users. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A103
Because motorcycles are small, may hide in blind spots and can be hard to judge for distance or speed, look for them with extra care. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A103
Before a left turn across an approaching motorcycle, look again and establish its presence and speed. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A103
Before turning in front of a signaling motorcycle, confirm it is actually turning because its indicator may have been left on. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A103
A motorcycle is entitled to a full traffic lane; do not move alongside it within the lane even if there appears to be room. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A104
Increase following room behind a motorcycle in rain or on slick pavement. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A104
Expect a motorcycle to change speed or direction for gravel, debris, seams, small animals or manhole covers that may barely affect a larger vehicle. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A104
Before entering or leaving a traffic lane or intersection, visually check mirrors and blind spots for motorcycles. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A104
Use indicators and brake lights to communicate turning, lane changes, merging, slowing and stopping to nearby motorcycle riders. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A104
Keep more than three seconds of following time behind a motorcycle. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A104
In general, larger trucks and buses have bigger blind spots, need more maneuvering room and take longer to stop or pass. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A105
Use extra care around snowplows because thrown snow can severely reduce visibility for close-following traffic. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A105
Stay out of a large vehicle's side and rear blind spots, and avoid spending long periods beside it. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A105
The handbook warns that when a following driver cannot see a large vehicle's mirrors, the large-vehicle driver cannot see that follower. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A105
Adjust the gap behind a large vehicle so most of the road ahead remains visible. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A105
When overtaking a large vehicle, keep speed steady and wait until its cab is visible in the rear-view mirror before returning to the lane. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A105
Give large vehicles extra room to accelerate and stop, and preserve their larger safety gap when merging back after a pass. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A105
The handbook's example gives a loaded truck with properly adjusted brakes a four-hundred-fifty-foot stop from fifty-five miles an hour on a dry road. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A106
Allow a large vehicle enough room for a sharp turn because it may need more than one lane. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A106
Do not squeeze past the right side of a large vehicle that angles left to make a right turn. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R33 | anchor: A106
Use extra caution near placarded hazardous-material vehicles and be ready to stop when following one toward a railroad crossing. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R34 | anchor: A106
On steep grades, expect slow large vehicles in the right lane of a four-lane road. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R35 | anchor: A106
Do not park in or near an escape or runaway ramp; it is reserved for stopping vehicles whose brakes have failed. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R36 | anchor: A106
Pilot vehicles are marked vehicles with amber lights that warn traffic about large loads and help those loads navigate road hazards. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R37 | anchor: A106
For an approaching pilot vehicle, slow and position as far right as possible. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R38 | anchor: A106
Increase following distance behind a pilot vehicle and use great care when passing it or the large load. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0106]

corpus_stability.reason: Corpus is the frozen July handbook snapshot; future issuer changes require a new source registration, rather than silent updates to this corpus.

verification_debt.claim_text: The first sharrow-purpose bullet begins on physical page one hundred one and completes on one hundred two with parked-door collision avoidance. The complete multi-page bullet is coverage debt; other complete purposes are locally sourced.

Sharrow and Bicycles May Use Full Lane visual recognition, and any other sharing-road illustrations in the mapped pages, have not received semantic image review. Text meanings are covered; image-based practice must wait.

Physical page one hundred six states that all hazardous-material vehicles stop at all railroad crossings. The following-driver preparedness rule is covered, but the universal legal classification and any statutory crossing or load exceptions require exact current official authority before being taught as universal.

Undated assertions about pedestrian fatality rates, cyclist collision injuries, motorcycle crash share, the most common cyclist crash type and truck-turn crash frequency lack study details in the mapped text. Their numeric or population rankings are withheld.
Physical page one hundred two lists a publication website, email and local-office access. Current contact functionality and availability were not checked; no access promise is made.
Physical page one hundred six says some load dimensions require pilot vehicles but gives no thresholds. No numerical permit or pilot requirement is invented.
